sources.title: DrivenData #306 DOE GEMS - Problem description
sources.used_for: Metric (kernel, TPw/FPw/FNw, alpha 0.2 / beta 0.8), submission format, rounds and prizes, training layers
sources.status: read-in-full (agent, one-off human-style read before the no-automation decision)
sources.evidence: Metric: DTI = TPw/(TPw + 0.2 FPw + 0.8 FNw + eps), k(d)=max(1-d/300 m,0); float32 single band in [0,1], NaN/null outside bounds; worked example 3.00/1.89/2.00 -> 0.60.

sources.used_for: Single GeoTIFF at 100 m, 3 submissions/week, one final submission, generative-AI disclosure, labels = INGENIOUS + expert-labelled new faults
sources.evidence: Rule A.1 gives 5:00 p.m. ET on the deadline date; the competition page says Dec 3, 2026 11:59 p.m. UTC - unresolved discrepancy (see irregularities).

sources.title: Berkowitz, Bour, Davy & Odling (2000) Scaling of fracture connectivity in geological formations. GRL 27(14), 2061-2064
sources.used_for: Connectivity framework for the topology candidate class (exponent a, fractal dimension D, density, critical length)
sources.status: abstract verified on publisher page; full text read via a ResearchGate copy
sources.evidence: Abstract: connectivity depends on scale of measurement for a < D+1, independent of scale for a > D+1; "Analysis of the San Andreas fault system shows that a < D+1 and that the connectivity threshold is reached only at a critical length scale." Text: a = 2.1, D = 1.65, beta = 0.0085; "connectivity is expected for L > 21 km"; "the above results are statistical, and provide connectivity estimates on averages, rather than on particular realizations".

sources.title: Faulds & Hinz (2015) Favorable tectonic and structural settings of geothermal systems in the Great Basin Region, Western USA. Proc. World Geothermal Congress
sources.used_for: Structural-setting statistics for step-overs, terminations, intersections; regional kinematic context
sources.evidence: Of ~250 categorised fields: step-overs/relay ramps ~32 %, normal-fault terminations 25 %, intersections 22 %, accommodation zones 9 %, transfer zones 5 %, pull-aparts 3 %, bends 2 %, major range-front faults 1 %; ~39 % of 426 systems are blind.

sources.title: Biasi & Wesnousky (2016) Steps and gaps in ground ruptures: empirical bounds on rupture propagation. BSSA 106, 1110-1124
sources.used_for: Scale (km) of step-overs relevant to linkage; motivates the 1-4 km candidate range as context only
sources.status: secondary quote only (article text on ResearchGate; primary paper by Wesnousky 2006 not read)
sources.evidence: "In Wesnousky (2006, 2008), the largest strike-slip step broken in rupture was 4 km." Concerns strike-slip earthquake ruptures, not mapped-fault connectivity.
